cluster_description: "With 12 of them managing to keep the card count at a meager 4.16 per game while the foul rate hovers near 20, it seems these refs are more concerned with documenting the chaos than actually stopping it, booking a player only when the foul count hits the mathematically perfect, yet utterly meaningless, 4.5 mark."

"With 12 of them managing to keep the card count at a meager 4.16 per game while the foul rate hovers near 20, it seems these refs are more concerned with documenting the chaos than actually stopping it, booking a player only when the foul count hits the mathematically perfect, yet utterly meaningless, 4.5 mark."

These 23 stewards of the whistle look less like arbiters of justice and more like a highly caffeinated committee whose main job is to ensure that for every 6 fouls committed, at least 3.35 of them end with a yellow card, ensuring the fouling rate is always roughly 6.4 times the card-giving rate.
"With 17 of them, and averaging nearly 25 fouls and 4.6 cards per game, these officials don't officiate matches—they run a yellow-card circus where every 5.4 fouls guarantees a man needs a nap."
